speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing jaundice, pruritus, weight loss, pale stools, and dark urine. These symptoms suggest a possible obstruction in the bile ducts. Can you tell me if you've had any recent abdominal pain or changes in your appetite?

speaker: Patient
text: 72-year-old male. The patient has experienced gradual yellow discoloration of the skin and generalized pruritus over the past 2 weeks. He also reports a decreased appetite and a weight loss of 6.3 kg (14 lb). The patient’s stool has been pale, and his urine is very dark. Three years ago, he had an episode of acute upper abdominal pain, which was managed with IV fluids, NSAIDs, and dietary modification. speaker: Doctor
text: Given your age, significant weight loss, and painless jaundice, I am concerned about pancreatic cancer. Has the abdominal pain you experienced three years ago recurred, or have you noticed any new pain in your upper abdomen or back?

speaker: Patient
text: has abstained from alcohol for these three years, after having consumed 1–2 beers daily for 40 years. He has a 50-year history of smoking a pack of cigarettes daily.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your significant smoking history and risk factors, I need to evaluate for pancreatic or biliary malignancy. REQUEST TEST: CT Abdomen_Pelvis

speaker: Doctor
text: A normal CT scan is unexpected given the signs of obstruction, so we must look closer at the biliary tree. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRCP demonstrates a markedly dilated common bile duct with an abrupt cutoff in the mid-portion. There is no evidence of filling defects such as stones or sludge within the visualized bile ducts. The pancreatic duct appears normal in caliber. The intrahepatic bile ducts are dilated.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRCP findings of an abrupt cutoff in the common bile duct without stones or pancreatic duct dilation strongly suggest a cholangiocarcinoma. DIAGNOSIS READY: Cholangiocarcinoma
